analysis.brief_en: A mobile petting zoo in North Carolina, Farm Adventures, is under scrutiny after four baby goats tested positive for rabies. The animals were likely exposed to the virus by a skunk that entered their pen in late July. Officials have confirmed three cases and assumed the fourth to be infected, leading to the euthanasia of all four goats to prevent further spread. The exposure risk spans multiple locations, including Durham County, Statesville, Lexington, Watauga County, Burke County, and Mocksville, with 10 sites potentially affected. Public health authorities are urging anyone who had contact with the goats to seek medical evaluation, as even saliva contact poses a risk. Farm Adventures has established a call center to assist concerned visitors. While no human rabies cases have been reported in North Carolina since 2011, preventive treatment is available for those exposed. The incident highlights the importance of vigilance with animals, even those that appear harmless.
